title: AI Must Enlarge the Economy, Not Divide It
gist: A teaser for a commentary arguing that AI's economic payoff depends on steering it toward augmenting workers rather than imitating them, and on rewriting incentives that currently favor capital over labor. It anchors the argument in the 'We Must Act Now' statement signed by 200-plus economists and AI researchers, including 16 Nobel laureates.

insights.claim: More than 200 economists and AI researchers, including 16 Nobel laureates, signed the 'We Must Act Now' statement warning that AI could reshape the global economy on a larger scale than the Industrial Revolution and far more quickly.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: An organized economist bloc pressing for AI labor-market intervention raises the odds of regulation or tax changes aimed at capital-biased automation; watch for policy proposals that shift AI capex economics.
insights.quote: More than 200 economists and AI researchers, including 16 Nobel laureates, have signed the We Must Act Now statement

insights.claim: Acknowledging that AI poses Industrial-Revolution-scale stakes does not by itself settle how AI should be developed, so signatory consensus on urgency masks unresolved disagreement on design choices.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Expect the AI policy fight to move from 'whether to act' to 'which development path to subsidize' — the contested ground where incentives and standards get set.
insights.quote: recognizing the stakes does not settle the question of how AI should be developed

insights.claim: AI should be steered toward complementing humans rather than imitating them, a distinction the authors argue is more consequential than it appears.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Frames a split between substitution-oriented AI vendors and augmentation-oriented tooling; policy tilting toward the latter would favor human-in-the-loop software over headcount-replacement pitches.
insights.quote: AI should be steered toward complementing humans rather than imitating them.
insights.locator: One of the statement's central claims

insights.claim: Unlocking AI's full economic potential requires replacing incentives that favor capital over labor with incentives that reward augmentation and investment in human capability.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Implies tax and subsidy regimes that currently make automating cheaper than upskilling are the policy lever to watch; changes there reprice automation-heavy business models.
insights.quote: replacing incentives that favor capital over labor with those that reward augmentation and investment in human capability
insights.locator: To unlock AI's full economic potential
